newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end 1/8 pt higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end 1/8 pt higher.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended up 1/8 point overall with spreads between high quality paper and lesser quality bonds narrowing as players hunted for yield.
"Any deal that's north of a 6.0, like lower-rated bonds, are just getting astronomical prices because people are just fighting for yield," a trader said, adding that supply remains light.
James Gammon, president of Lebenthal Asset Management, also cited a paper shortage.
"We need more bonds," Gammon said. "There's such a shortage of them, which is why we are so rich versus Treasuries."

While New York City is expected to sell $750 million of general obligation bonds on Wednesday, Gammon lamented that the maturities only run to 2016. He would rather the deal offered maturities in the 2020s, allowing him to pick up some yield, the portfolio manager said.
Never-the-less, Gammon predicted the deal will trigger a "feeding frenzy" among retail investors.
"Next week the New York City deal is going to be eaten alive with the intermediate maturities," Gammon said.

Meanwhile, in the secondary market on Thursday, a municipal analyst said while the overall muni cash market closed up 1/8, dollar bonds were down 1/8 to 1/4 shortly after release of April consumer price index data.

The Labor Department said the consumer price index for April rose 0.1 percent, and increased 0.3 percent at the core. The figure was almost in line with economists' expectations, which pegged the overall figure at up 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent higher at the core.
Dollar bonds came back to about even by noon, then added 1/8 point before the session's end. A trader earlier attributed the uptick to industrial production and capacity utilization data.

The Federal Reserve's industrial production figure April, was unchanged from March and below the expectations of a 0.2 percent rise. Capacity utilization was 83.4 percent, compared to expectations for 84.1 percent.
The analyst said high-grade issues ended slightly firmer, improving a basis point or two through the intermediate range. Activity was light.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed up 8/32 at 116-10/32. The June T-bond contract closed up 5/32 at 110-10/32. The MOB spread was 192 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 7/32 at 96-30/32 to yield 6.87 percent in late New York trade.

Thursday's new issue action saw Smith Barney Inc reprice $37 million Oregon State Board of Education bonds, raising yields in several maturities. The top yield in 2027 was raised to 5.70 percent from 5.65 percent.
Earlier, Prudential Securities Inc won $60 million of Montgomery County, Pa., general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 5.3975 percent.
Looking ahead to next week, negotitated and competive new issues area expected to total $2.44 billion.
Lehman Brothers is slated to bring the $750 million New York City GO on Wednesday. The offering, the week's largest, is one of 29 scheduled negotiated issues totaling $1.5 billion.
Tuesday's $285 million Nevada offering is the largest scheduled competive offering. Seventy-seven competitive issues totaling $924 million are scheduled next week.
((--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655))
